evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: a dark slate core of dense nodes sits inside a khaki-lit outer shell with rose tips at the top; by shot-20s the same dark core persists at a smaller scale, so the flow threshold effect is visible on screen.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: one 2D scene with a growing L-system of several hundred nodes, halos, a flow dial and a dark/lit state change; no depth, lighting or material layers beyond flat fills.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: restrained khaki-green ground with celadon branches and tan nodes, centred and clean; shot-08s: the dark core is an even dot grid with little tonal variation and the halos are barely visible.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: a branching fan in celadon and tan on khaki-green with dark slate nodes; the recent Penrose tiling and sand-grid nights use hard-edged tiles, so this branching form and palette differ.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: composed centred fan with the dial at 10 cm/s; shot-20s: a pull-back to a smaller colony with the dial still at 25 cm/s, so flow does not visibly ease back and the end state is only partly resolved.

pairwise_justification: Shot-08s shows a dark core inside a lit shell, which reads as a changing scene. The median's Penrose kites are a strong static tiling, but tonight's threshold shift wins a head-to-head on legibility and palette.

critique.change: Make the flow dial ease back by shot-20s: it reads 25 cm/s in both shot-08s and shot-20s, so the core never reopens. Drop the dial to about 15 cm/s by 20s and thin the dark core so the reopening is visible.
Break the uniform dot grid in the dark core: vary node radius and slate tone by live-neighbour count so the core reads as a shelter gradient rather than a flat dot cloud, especially at shot-08s.
Make the boundary-layer halos visible at shot-02s and shot-08s, with a khaki haze between tight branches, so the second mechanism adds a layer beyond flat node fills.
